quests.instruction: The story has a main thread and a side thread. Choose the three statements that carry the main thread across both paragraphs, in order.
quests.story:
Nadia's neighbourhood association wanted to turn an empty lot into a small playground. They asked the council for permission and were told they needed a safety inspection first, which would cost four hundred pounds. Nadia started a sponsored walk to raise the money.

Forty people joined the walk and raised five hundred pounds. The inspector visited in March and approved the site with two small changes, and volunteers built the playground in May. Meanwhile a dispute over who owned the fence at the edge of the lot was settled by the council in a single letter.
options: After the inspection was passed, volunteers built the playground in May.
Nadia's sponsored walk raised £500.
A dispute over who owned the fence at the edge of the lot was settled by a single council letter.
The council required a £400 safety inspection before allowing a playground on the empty lot.
quests.hint: Look for the thread that starts in the first paragraph and ends in the second.
quests.explanation: The fence dispute has its own resolution and doesn't help or block the playground. The main thread is the required inspection, the fundraising walk, and the building of the playground.
storyKeyEvents: The council required a £400 safety inspection before allowing a playground on the empty lot.
Nadia's sponsored walk raised £500.
After the inspection was passed, volunteers built the playground in May.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give the most complete compressed summary of both paragraphs, in order.
quests.story:
Hamza had moved to the city for a job in the autumn. The flat he rented was small but had a view of the river. His manager asked him to lead a training day for new staff, and Hamza had never taught anyone before.

He asked a colleague, Pilar, to watch a practice run and give notes. She suggested cutting the slides in half and adding two exercises. On the day the new staff stayed engaged all morning, and two of them thanked him afterwards.
options: Hamza rented a small flat with a view of the river after moving to the city for his job.
Hamza, who had never taught before, was asked to lead a training day for new staff.
On the day the new staff stayed engaged all morning.
A colleague, Pilar, watched a practice run and suggested halving the slides and adding two exercises.
quests.hint: Setting details in the opening paragraph aren't always part of the main thread.
quests.explanation: The flat and its view describe where Hamza lives but play no part in the training day. The summary needs the request, the practice run and its advice, and the engaged staff.
storyKeyEvents: Hamza, who had never taught before, was asked to lead a training day for new staff.
A colleague, Pilar, watched a practice run and suggested halving the slides and adding two exercises.
On the day the new staff stayed engaged all morning.

quests.instruction: The story has a main thread and a side thread. Choose the three statements that carry the main thread across both paragraphs, in order.
quests.story:
The bookshop café had been losing money for months. The owner, Carlota, noticed that most customers left after one coffee. She replaced the small tables with two long shared ones.

Within a month strangers were chatting over the tables, and many stayed for a second drink. Separately, the shop raised its book prices by five per cent. By spring the café was making a small profit.
options: The café returned to profit because the shop raised its book prices.
She replaced the small tables with two long shared ones.
Customers stayed for second drinks, and by spring the café made a small profit.
Carlota noticed the café was losing money because most customers left after one coffee.
quests.hint: Check which event the story links to the café's recovery, not just which came before it.
quests.explanation: The price rise is a separate change in the shop, and the story ties the café's recovery to the shared tables and the second drinks. Linking the profit to the prices reverses the story's cause.
storyKeyEvents: Carlota noticed the café was losing money because most customers left after one coffee.
She replaced the small tables with two long shared ones.
Customers stayed for second drinks, and by spring the café made a small profit.

quests.story:
Tuva's jazz trio lost its piano when the church sold it. Tuva asked members to bring ideas, and a garage, a library and the music school two streets away were suggested. She wrote to the music school offering to pay a small hourly fee.

The school agreed to lend a room and a piano on Thursday evenings for half the fee she offered. The trio rehearsed there all winter, and in December it played at the school's open evening, where two new members joined.
options: The trio lost its piano when the church sold it.
The music school agreed to lend a room and piano on Thursday evenings for half the fee offered.
The trio played at the school's open evening in December and two new members joined.
Members suggested a garage, a library and the music school as places to rehearse.

quests.explanation: The garage and library were only ideas, and the story follows the music school. The main thread is the lost piano, the school's offer, and the December performance.
storyKeyEvents: The trio lost its piano when the church sold it.
The music school agreed to lend a room and piano on Thursday evenings for half the fee offered.
The trio played at the school's open evening in December and two new members joined.

quests.instruction: The story has a main thread and a side thread. Choose the three statements that carry the main thread across both paragraphs, in order.
quests.story:
The town's swimming club needed a new coach after Mr. Bell retired. The committee advertised the post and interviewed three candidates. They chose Ms. Ferro, who had coached a county team for six years.

In her first month she rearranged the lanes by speed rather than age, and times improved across the club. Mr. Bell, meanwhile, moved to the coast and took up sailing.
options: Ms. Ferro rearranged the lanes by speed, and times improved across the club.
The committee interviewed three candidates after Mr. Bell retired.
Mr. Bell, the retired coach, moved to the coast and took up sailing.
They chose Ms. Ferro, an experienced county coach.

quests.explanation: Mr. Bell's move follows his retirement but doesn't affect the club's new coach or its swimmers. The main thread is the search, the choice of Ms. Ferro, and the improved times.
storyKeyEvents: The committee interviewed three candidates after Mr. Bell retired.
They chose Ms. Ferro, an experienced county coach.
Ms. Ferro rearranged the lanes by speed, and times improved across the club.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give the most complete compressed summary of both paragraphs, in order.
quests.story:
Ansgar's bike was stolen from outside the library on Monday. He reported it to the police and posted a photo on the neighbourhood group.

On Thursday a neighbour spotted it locked outside a café across town. Ansgar confirmed the frame number, and the police recovered it. He bought a stronger lock that same week.
options: After buying a stronger lock, Ansgar posted a photo of the bike.
Ansgar reported the stolen bike to the police and posted a photo on the neighbourhood group.
A neighbour spotted the bike locked outside a café across town.
After Ansgar confirmed the frame number, the police recovered it.
quests.hint: Check the order across the two paragraphs.
quests.explanation: The lock was bought after the bike was found, while the photo was posted right after the theft. Reversing them puts the end of the story before its beginning.
storyKeyEvents: Ansgar reported the stolen bike to the police and posted a photo on the neighbourhood group.
A neighbour spotted the bike locked outside a café across town.
After Ansgar confirmed the frame number, the police recovered it.

quests.instruction: The story has a main thread and a side thread. Choose the three statements that carry the main thread across both paragraphs, in order.
quests.story:
The village shop's sales fell in the spring. Its owner, Yara, suspected the new supermarket nearby, but a customer survey said people mostly wanted longer opening hours. Yara decided to open until eight instead of six.

In the first month sales rose by a fifth, especially between six and eight. The supermarket, meanwhile, had cut its prices that same month.
options: The village shop's sales fell in the spring.
Sales rose because the supermarket cut its prices.
In the first month sales rose by a fifth, especially between six and eight.
A survey showed people wanted longer hours, so Yara opened until eight.
quests.hint: Look at when the extra sales happened to see what they came from.
quests.explanation: The extra sales came mostly between six and eight, the new hours, so the supermarket's price cut can't explain them. The summary follows the drop, the survey and the change, and the rise.
storyKeyEvents: The village shop's sales fell in the spring.
A survey showed people wanted longer hours, so Yara opened until eight.
In the first month sales rose by a fifth, especially between six and eight.

options: He finished in four hours and eleven minutes and signed up for next year's race.

Lior trained for a year to run a marathon in under four hours.
Lior finished the marathon in under four hours.

storyKeyEvents: Lior trained for a year to run a marathon in under four hours.
Cramp slowed him after thirty kilometres on race day.
He finished in four hours and eleven minutes and signed up for next year's race.

Mr. Ito put a display near the door and mentioned the scheme in the newsletter.
By June the tools were being borrowed sixty times a month.

When he switched it on, the radio crackled and then played a station clearly. Kwame sat for a while listening and thinking of how his father used to hum along. He gave the radio to his father for his birthday.
options: Kwame gave the restored radio to his father for his birthday.
Kwame sat listening for a while and thought of how his father used to hum along to it.
Kwame spent three weekends restoring his father's old radio.
When he switched it on, the radio crackled and then played a station clearly.

storyKeyEvents: Kwame spent three weekends restoring his father's old radio.
When he switched it on, the radio crackled and then played a station clearly.
Kwame gave the restored radio to his father for his birthday.

With the shelves cleared, the window display improved and sales rose by ten per cent.

options: Elif proposed a shared document with a section for each person in her group's joint report.

Elif merged the sections and the lecturer said the report read as a single argument.

The shelter stayed dry because the council installed a new timetable board.
The engineer found that the drainage channel had been fitted backwards.
A contractor refitted the channel, and the shelter stayed dry in the next rainfall.

quests.explanation: A timetable board has nothing to do with rain running into the shelter. The dry shelter follows the engineer's finding and the refitted channel.
storyKeyEvents: The shelter on Hill Road was often wet inside, and commuters complained to the council.
The engineer found that the drainage channel had been fitted backwards.
A contractor refitted the channel, and the shelter stayed dry in the next rainfall.

Noise fell noticeably on those floors.
The tenants raised money and fitted mats on all six floors by the summer.

options: The old watch shop was losing customers to online sellers.
Pedro started a website offering repairs by post.
Pedro's cousin, who used to work at the shop, opened a bakery in another town.

Within six months half of the shop's income came from postal repairs.

options: The daughter slept in the bigger room before Wanda had measured the rooms.

The daughter wanted a bigger room, but the family couldn't afford to move.

storyKeyEvents: The daughter wanted a bigger room, but the family couldn't afford to move.
Wanda measured the rooms and worked out that the box room and the study could swap.
After a weekend of moving furniture, the daughter slept in the bigger room by Sunday evening.

The director sent a reminder and blocked calendars after some managers ignored the rule.
After two months a survey showed staff felt less rushed.
